title: Microsoft Weighs 20% Cost Cuts In Azure Vertical Amid Soaring AI Data Center Spending: Report
source_used: Stocktwits' account of The Information's report, read on Yahoo Finance
key_facts: The Information reported, citing people familiar with the matter, that Girish Bablani, president of Azure's software development group, told team leaders to identify ways to cut expenses by at least 20%.
His division has about 11,500 people; the savings aim to offset heavy AI data-centre capital spending and fund higher pay to keep staff from rivals such as Meta and Anthropic.
Measures are under consideration and could include parting ways with external contractors; the report did not say whether job cuts could follow.
A Microsoft spokesperson said 'Azure leadership has not directed teams to develop cost-cutting plans' and that every responsible company prepares for a range of scenarios.
Azure revenue was $101.9 billion in the 12 months to June, up 40%, about 31% of Microsoft's total; June-quarter revenue rose 43%.
Amazon Web Services and Oracle have also cut staff to protect cash flow amid rising AI costs (Stocktwits).
Separately, Microsoft reshuffled its cloud leadership, giving executive Arun Ulag wider oversight including Azure Core, which serves clients such as OpenAI.
quote_evidence: Girish Bablani, president of Azure's software development group, instructed team leaders to identify ways to lower expenses by at least 20%, The Information reported.
Azure leadership has not directed teams to develop cost-cutting plans.

While the exact measures remain under consideration and could include parting ways with external contractors, the report did not state categorically whether internal discussions could lead to staff layoffs.
why_it_matters_hint: Heavy AI data-centre spending is reported to be pushing even Microsoft's growing cloud unit to look for cost cuts, which Microsoft denies.
notes: Stocktwits article syndicated on Yahoo Finance; The Information's original (paywalled) was not opened. Microsoft's denial is quoted from the spokesperson as reported by The Information.
